correctness.rationale: Fix an order of the A-vertices and concatenate their incident-edge blocks. Simplicity makes each B-side sequence independent of internal block permutations. At a left vertex of degree d, properness gives d! distinct local sequences while its d neighbours forbid at most d; d!>d for d>=3. The block choices are independent, proving the universal claim.
correctness.risk: The proof uses simplicity and proper edge-colouring and does not cover nonbipartite low-degree cases.

A local-lemma criterion for sequential edge orderings in bipartite graphs

value.risk: Its value is the exact class-wide threshold rather than technical depth.

final_claim: For every finite simple bipartite graph \(G=(A,B;E)\) with a fixed proper edge-colouring, if every \(a\in A\) has degree at least \(3\), then a global edge order distinguishes the incident-colour sequences at the ends of every edge; hence every finite simple \(d\)-regular bipartite graph is sequentially orderable for all \(d\ge3\).
limitations: No nonbipartite degree-3/4/5 claim is made.
